title: Italy regulator probes AI music startup Suno over terms of service
key_facts: Italy's competition authority, the AGCM, said on 6 Oct 2026 that Suno's terms 'may be unfair' under Article 33 of the Consumer Code.
Concerns: unilateral changes to prices and service, account termination without notice, broad liability limits, and extra terms users cannot see before signing up.
The content licence is called insufficiently defined and requires users to waive moral rights, contrary to Italy's copyright law (Law 633/1941).
Disputes must go to binding individual US arbitration with a class-action waiver and Massachusetts courts.
The AGCM will open a public consultation in the coming weeks.
Its fining powers over unfair contract terms run from 5,000 euros to 10 million euros.
Suno's current terms took effect 3 Sep 2026; UMG and Sony filed a second copyright suit against it on 18 Sep 2026.
quote_evidence: Italy's competition authority has opened an investigation into Suno's terms of service.
The AGCM said it will open a public consultation on Suno's terms on the authority's website "over the next few weeks."
why_it_matters_hint: The regulator is testing whether an AI music service's contract terms are fair to European users.
notes: Reuters article returned 401; MBW's report of the AGCM statement was read, and The News International carries the same facts.
